cards.hint: Focus on what steady descent does to height.
options: it loses altitude as it travels
cards.quote: If a glider is in a steady (constant velocity and no acceleration) descent, it loses altitude as it travels.
cards.stem: What happens during steady descent with constant velocity?

cards.hint: Think about which force steady flight must balance.
cards.quote: The lift L times the cosine cos of the glide angle plus the drag D times the sine sin of the glide angle is equal to the weight W
cards.stem: In steady flight, what do the lift and drag parts combine to balance?

cards.hint: Recall how lift and drag terms are paired.
options: drag times the cosine of the glide angle
cards.quote: The lift times the sine of the glide angle is equal to the drag times the cosine of the glide angle.
cards.stem: What does lift times sine balance in the other force relation?

cards.hint: Recall what makes this aircraft special.
cards.quote: A glider is a special kind of aircraft that has no engine.
cards.stem: What defines this special kind of aircraft?
